title: AO/59/2007 of MAHESH SINGH RANA Vs GOPI RAM AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Appeal From Order No. 59 of 2007
Mahesh Singh Rana
Ö..Plaintiff/Appellant
Versus
Gopi Ram and others
 ......Ö.Respondents
Present:
Mr. Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate assisted by Mrs. Indu Sharma,
Advocate for the plaintiff/appellant.
Mr. N.S. Bisht, Advocate holding brief of Mr. M.S. Tyagi, Advocate for
the respondents.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Plaintiff has filed suit for permanent prohibitory
injunction on the strength of sale deed dated
13.10.2006, however, application for seeking ad
interim injunction was rejected by the Trial Court.
Feeling aggrieved, plaintiff/appellant has preferred the
present appeal.
This Court while admitting the appeal was
pleased to direct the parties to maintain status quo,
vide order dated 23.2.2007.
Undisputedly, meanwhile, defendants/
respondents, herein, filed another suit for cancellation
of sale deed dated 13.10.2006 being relied upon by
the plaintiff/appellant, herein, in the present suit,
however, suit for cancellation of sale deed was
dismissed on 20.5.2013. Therefore, prima facie, sale
deed in favour of the plaintiff stands good showing
prima facie title in favour of the plaintiff. If prima facie
title is proved in favour of the plaintiff, then balance of

2
convenience can be said in favour of the plaintiff, and
in the event nature of property is changed during the
pendency of the suit by any means, it can be said that
there would be irreparable loss to the plaintiff.
Therefore, in the peculiar facts and
circumstances of the case, present appeal stands
disposed of with the direction that parties shall
maintain status quo during the pendency of the suit.
It is further directed that learned Trial Court shall
explore every possibility to decide the suit at its own
merit in accordance with law, preferably within one
year from the date a copy of this order is placed before
the learned Trial Court.
It goes without saying that while deciding the
suit, the learned Trial Court shall not be prejudiced
from any observations recorded hereinbefore.
No order as to costs.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 8.5.2014
Avneet
